keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Lotharingia row; its Kingdom of Germany and Holy Roman Empire shapes draw all of it as imperial). The duchy is the northern half of the divided Lotharingia; the pages give no border, so Belgium, the Netherlands and a 45 km circle each around Aachen and Cologne are the reading (about 87,000 km2, including Frisia in the north, which the page makes lordships only in 1524-36). The infobox gives no area. Repair of 2026-10-25 (review, blocking): the shape is no longer all of Belgium. The Duchy of Lower Lorraine page's lead has the duchy 'encompassing almost all of modern Netherlands' and covering Belgium, Luxembourg and parts of Germany and France, so Luxembourg is added; the Brabant page has only 'imperial lands up to the Schelde river in the west' coming under Baldwin V of Flanders by 1059, so Crown Flanders west of the Scheldt (West Flanders, and East Flanders west of the river) is taken out of every shape. The Lower Lorraine page is silent on the Scheldt and on any French-held Flanders; the polygon along Tournai, Oudenaarde and Ghent is the researcher's reading of the river, and the Tournaisis in Hainaut west of the Scheldt is cut by the same polygon only inside East Flanders (it stays in the shape, soft).

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The two pages disagree on the first duke (Godfrey of Mons (Hainaut) on the Lower Lorraine page, Godfrey of Jülich on the Brabant page) and the Lower Lorraine page has no area, capital or dukes before 1012. eu-07's duchy-of-lotharingia dossier gave the successor land as Lotharingia minus Lorraine, which includes Alsace in the gazetteer; this dossier uses Belgium, the Netherlands and circles at Aachen and Cologne instead. Not settled: the Rhineland border (Cologne, Aachen, Jülich, Cleves), Frisia and Utrecht's status, the dukes 959-1012, Hainaut and Namur as counties inside the duchy, the Brabant landgraviate of 1085. wars is empty: no war on the pages moved the border. Counterparts needing dossiers: duchy-of-lorraine (Upper Lorraine before 1431; eu-09 starts at 1431), county-of-flanders (eu-10), Bishopric of Liège. Gazetteer lacks Bouillon and Ghent (coordinates used).

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) shape: Belgium minus Crown Flanders (West Flanders and East Flanders west of the Scheldt, by a polygon along Tournai-Oudenaarde-Ghent), plus Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the Aachen and Cologne circles; the Lower Lorraine page lead was re-read (Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, parts of Germany and France) and is silent on the Scheldt, Aachen and the French part of Flanders; the Brabant page gives 'Imperial lands up to the Schelde river in the west' by 1059. Not cut: the Tournaisis and the Zeeuws-Vlaanderen strip south of the Western Scheldt (the page is silent), Hainaut west of the Scheldt. (2) Losses: Liège in 980 (Liège page: secular powers 980, Notker) and Utrecht in 1024 (Utrecht page: princes of the Empire 1024), with new keyframes; the two bishopric dossiers' found events name holy-roman-empire and should name this duchy instead (not touched). The Lower Lorraine page lists both bishoprics among fiefs that came to imperial immediacy but dates neither and does not name Notker or 1024. (3) Counterpart of the 1033 gain and 1044 loss is now duchy-of-upper-lorraine (Upper Lorraine 959-1431 needs a dossier; the Cliopatria row duchy-of-lorraine starts in 1431). (4) Routing to eu-10: county-of-brabant and county-of-holland start in 1260, so the land is undrawn 1190-1259. Four pages are now used of the 2-5 budget.
